subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should foreground replies ever wait for memoryFlush/preflight compaction, or should compaction move to an isolated/background lane with a bounded foreground handoff?
rationale: The current foreground path protects session consistency by serializing work, and changing that behavior affects session-state ordering, transcript writes, message delivery, and recovery semantics beyond a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design foreground-safe compaction
options.body: Move or split compaction and memoryFlush so user messages are not starved, while explicitly preserving session/transcript ownership and adding lane-drain regression proof.

options.title: Keep foreground compaction with shorter recovery
options.body: Accept session serialization as the product contract and focus on shorter timeouts, notices, and diagnostic abort/release behavior instead of true lane isolation.

options.title: Close as mitigated
options.body: Treat the 180-second default timeout and diagnostic recovery as sufficient, leaving explicit longer user timeouts and foreground blocking as accepted behavior.

recommendation.title: Design foreground-safe compaction
recommendation.body: Move or split compaction and memoryFlush so user messages are not starved, while explicitly preserving session/transcript ownership and adding lane-drain regression proof.
